standard.title: Evaluate critical feedback in visual arts practice
standard.description: evaluate critical feedback when planning, developing and refining their visual arts practice
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have created planned artworks using coordinated visual choices and can explain their decisions (AC9AVA8C01/AC9AVA8C02, implied from progression). They have engaged with peer and teacher feedback at an informal level. They have not yet systematically evaluated feedback, tracked its influence on decision-making, or distinguished between seeking impressions and confirming intended responses.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students evaluate critical feedback from teachers, peers and audiences when planning, developing and refining their visual arts practice — documenting how feedback influences decisions.

nodes.label: Seeking impressions without leading
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can seek feedback in a way that uncovers genuine audience impressions rather than confirming their own intended response.
nodes.minimum_width: Seek feedback on one work in progress without revealing the intended meaning first; record what the audience perceived.
nodes.typical_width: Develop and use feedback-seeking strategies that uncover meaning and interpretation without confirming or leading the audience; compare audience impressions with intended response; use the gap as a diagnostic tool.
wider: Design a structured feedback protocol for the class — develop questions that elicit genuine impression without leading, test it on peer works, and evaluate the protocol's effectiveness
Seek feedback from an audience outside the class (community group, exhibition visitors) — compare impressions from different audience types and reflect on what this reveals
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who lead audiences toward their intended meaning receive confirmation rather than feedback — the gap between intention and reception is diagnostic only if the seeking process is neutral. Without this, subsequent evaluation of feedback is based on affirming data, not useful critique.

response_modes.reason: The distinction between 'seeking impressions' and 'leading the audience' is subtle and requires explicit instruction and practice. Scaffolding the feedback protocol — what questions to ask and what not to say — builds the skill.

success_criteria: Seeks feedback on a work without revealing the intended meaning first
Records what the audience perceived and compares this with the intended response

nodes.label: Evaluating and responding to feedback
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate feedback from teachers and peers and document how it influences their decisions — accepting, adapting or consciously setting aside feedback with reasoning.
nodes.minimum_width: Evaluate at least one piece of feedback on a work in progress; document one decision made in response to it — including whether they accepted, adapted or set it aside and why.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate and respond to feedback from multiple sources across multiple works; document decisions and reasoning in written, oral or multimedia journal; track changes made as a result of feedback; use self-assessment with Viewpoints questions alongside external feedback.
wider: Collaborate with a community group or external agency to generate ideas and receive feedback on an artwork project — evaluate how external feedback differs from peer/teacher feedback
Develop a systematic reflective process — use Viewpoints questions to self-assess work in progress alongside external feedback and document the relationship between the two

response_modes.reason: Evaluating feedback requires weighing its validity against intentions — students need a reasoning framework (Does this align with my intent? Is this a perception issue or an execution issue? Should I change the work or my communication of it?) rather than simply accepting all feedback.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: External collaboration feedback — from community groups or curated exhibition contexts — provides genuinely different perspectives from classroom feedback, substantially expanding students' understanding of how their work communicates beyond the familiar school context.
success_criteria: Evaluates at least one piece of feedback on a work in progress
Documents a decision made in response — including whether it was accepted, adapted or set aside, with a reason

nodes.label: Structuring ideas and tracking development
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use structured documentation (sketches, maquettes, annotated digital images, journals) to experiment with ways of developing ideas and to track the evolution of a work.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least one structured documentation form (sketch series, annotated images, journal) to show how an idea evolved through at least two stages.
nodes.typical_width: Experiment with and evaluate ways of structuring ideas in sketches, studies, maquettes, annotated digital images and journals; use documentation to track development and refine directions; connect documentation to feedback evaluation.
wider: Create a virtual or scale model of an exhibition of a researched artist — use this structure to communicate your understanding of the artist's intentions and refine it based on feedback
Plan and document a substantial creative project from initial idea through to completed work — use the documentation to evaluate the role of feedback at each stage

response_modes.reason: Documentation, feedback evaluation and iterative refinement come together here — students demonstrate a coherent creative process where external critique informs internal development at every stage.

success_criteria: Uses at least one structured documentation form to show how an idea evolved through two or more stages
Connects at least one documented change to a feedback evaluation
